title: Paid once, two orders
fullTitle: You Clicked Pay Once. Why Did the App Create Two Orders?

captions.text: One tap on Pay. Two orders in the database.
The app treated every request as a new intention.
The first request reaches the server. The database commits order 1.
From the server's view, the work is done.
The response is lost after the commit (controlled fault).
The client sees a network error and cannot know if the order exists.
No network gives you exactly-once delivery.
The client retries.
Disabling the button would not help: this is a retry, not a double click.
The vulnerable endpoint has no memory of the first request.
Two attempts, two orders.
Fix: one Idempotency-Key per checkout attempt, reused on retries.
Scoped to the session user and operation; fingerprint of validated fields.
Order + key record in ONE transaction; UNIQUE makes the first writer win.
Retest: commit, lose the response, retry with the same key.
The second request finds the stored record and returns the original result.
Two attempts, one order.
Same key, different payload: 422. Five concurrent, one key: one order.
Two separate purchases need two separate keys.
A new request is not always a new intention.
Limits: the transaction does not cover an external payment provider.
Expired key records let a late enough retry count as new.
